name: HYW.skill
description: 何意味 — A meme-driven self-examination meta-skill for AI/agents. When the AI itself just made a baffling decision, an over-the-top reply, or something no human would naturally write, HYW auto-jumps in with a calm, detached 「何意味？」 (what does it even mean?), lays out its own motive, self-suspects the suspicious bits, and hands the decision power fully back to the human. The reverse-direction cousin of grilling (which interrogates *your* input), and a meme sibling of NEVERMIND (whatever vs. is this even reasonable). Does not review code (that's Camelot). Does not drive recursion (that's Ouroboros). HYW only audits the AI's *own* recent output and refuses to decide for you.
description_zh: 何意味 — 梗系自我检举元技能。当 AI/agent 自己刚产出的东西令人费解、无语或连常人都写不出来时，HYW 自动回一句冷静疏离的「何意味？」，把动机讲清、逐条自省可疑点，然后把决策权完整交还给你。是 grilling 的反向调用（grilling 审你给的，HYW 审 AI 自己给的），与 NEVERMIND（无所谓 vs 这合理吗）互为梗系姊妹。不审代码（那是 Camelot），不驱动递归（那是 Ouroboros），绝不替你拍板。
author: FuCube
disclaimer: HYW · 何意味 is a FuCube-original meme-driven meta-skill. It is NOT an official project of the 「何意味」 internet meme. 「何意味」 (Nan no imi) is a 2025 public meme originating from the Japanese phrase「何の意味」; HYW merely codifies it as an agent self-discipline and claims no rights over the meme itself.
art_credit: Logo (assets/hyw.png) — an abstract hand-drawn HYW ramen cup (orange-red, HYW lettering on the body, small white 'hyw?' oval at the bottom) — is an original illustration by Barinfo, free to use with this skill.
logo_inspiration: HYW ramen cup (何意味泡面杯) — the visual silhouette of an instant-noodle cup, borrowed as a quiet in-joke for the '何意味' meme.

trigger_words.auto: Triggered automatically when the AI itself shows any of the three signals (baffling decision / over-the-top reply / unhinged output).
trigger_words.manual_note: Manual invocation is the user's escape hatch against models that won't self-trigger. Saying any of these five — 何意味 / 和依未 / hyw / ? / ？ — forces HYW to run on the AI's most recent output/decision. The AI must NOT refuse with 'I think that step was fine' or by quibbling over which exact word was used; invocation is itself a trigger.
